events.title: Massacre of Huguenots at Wassy sparks the French Wars of Religion
events.description: Troops escorting the Duke of Guise attacked Protestants worshipping in a barn at Wassy, killing some 50 to 60. The killings set off more than three decades of religious civil war in France.
events.html: Troops escorting the Duke of Guise attacked Protestants worshipping in a barn at Wassy, killing some 50 to 60. The killings set off more than three decades of religious civil war in France.

events.title: Salem witch trial examinations begin
events.description: Magistrates questioned Sarah Good, Sarah Osborne and the enslaved woman Tituba in Salem Village, Massachusetts. Accusations spread, and by autumn twenty people had been executed.
events.html: Magistrates questioned Sarah Good, Sarah Osborne and the enslaved woman Tituba in Salem Village, Massachusetts. Accusations spread, and by autumn twenty people had been executed.

events.title: Articles of Confederation come into force
events.description: Maryland's ratification brought into effect the first constitution of the United States. The weak confederation lacked powers to tax and was replaced by the Constitution in 1789.
events.html: Maryland's ratification brought into effect the first constitution of the United States. The weak confederation lacked powers to tax and was replaced by the Constitution in 1789.

events.title: Napoleon lands in France after escaping Elba
events.description: Napoleon came ashore at Golfe-Juan near Cannes with about a thousand men. Troops sent to stop him joined him instead, and he entered Paris on 20 March to begin the Hundred Days.
events.html: Napoleon came ashore at Golfe-Juan near Cannes with about a thousand men. Troops sent to stop him joined him instead, and he entered Paris on 20 March to begin the Hundred Days.

events.title: Texas convention assembles at Washington-on-the-Brazos
events.description: Delegates from across Texas met in a half-built hall to decide the province's future while the Alamo was under siege. The next day they declared independence from Mexico.
events.html: Delegates from across Texas met in a half-built hall to decide the province's future while the Alamo was under siege. The next day they declared independence from Mexico.

events.title: Yellowstone becomes the world's first national park
events.description: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the act setting aside Yellowstone's geysers and canyons 'for the benefit and enjoyment of the people'. The national park idea spread around the world.
events.html: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the act setting aside Yellowstone's geysers and canyons 'for the benefit and enjoyment of the people'. The national park idea spread around the world.

events.title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at the Battle of Adwa
events.description: Emperor Menelik II's army routed an Italian invasion force in northern Ethiopia. The victory forced Italy to recognise Ethiopian independence and became a lasting symbol of African resistance.
events.html: Emperor Menelik II's army routed an Italian invasion force in northern Ethiopia. The victory forced Italy to recognise Ethiopian independence and became a lasting symbol of African resistance.

events.title: Henri Becquerel discovers radioactivity
events.description: Becquerel found that uranium salts left in a drawer had fogged a photographic plate without any sunlight. He had discovered radioactivity, soon investigated by Marie and Pierre Curie.
events.html: Becquerel found that uranium salts left in a drawer had fogged a photographic plate without any sunlight. He had discovered radioactivity, soon investigated by Marie and Pierre Curie.

events.title: Koreans rise against Japanese rule in the March 1st Movement
events.description: A declaration of independence was read in Seoul, and peaceful demonstrations spread across Korea. Japanese forces suppressed them, killing thousands, but the movement inspired Korean nationalism.
events.html: A declaration of independence was read in Seoul, and peaceful demonstrations spread across Korea. Japanese forces suppressed them, killing thousands, but the movement inspired Korean nationalism.

events.title: International Monetary Fund begins operations
events.description: Created at the Bretton Woods conference of 1944, the IMF opened for business in Washington. It was designed to stabilise exchange rates and lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulties.
events.html: Created at the Bretton Woods conference of 1944, the IMF opened for business in Washington. It was designed to stabilise exchange rates and lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulties.

events.title: Castle Bravo, the largest US nuclear test, contaminates the Pacific
events.description: The hydrogen bomb tested at Bikini Atoll yielded 15 megatons, far more than predicted. Fallout sickened Marshall Islanders and the crew of the Japanese fishing boat Lucky Dragon No. 5.
events.html: The hydrogen bomb tested at Bikini Atoll yielded 15 megatons, far more than predicted. Fallout sickened Marshall Islanders and the crew of the Japanese fishing boat Lucky Dragon No. 5.

events.title: US Supreme Court bans the execution of juvenile offenders
events.description: In Roper v. Simmons the Court ruled five to four that executing people for crimes committed under 18 was cruel and unusual punishment. The decision spared some 70 people on death row.
events.html: In Roper v. Simmons the Court ruled five to four that executing people for crimes committed under 18 was cruel and unusual punishment. The decision spared some 70 people on death row.
